subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup failure policy should OpenClaw own when active SecretRef exec providers fail under launchd/systemd restart loops?
rationale: The current behavior is documented fail-fast startup, but the report shows side-effecting credential-provider retries can exhaust external account-wide secret access; changing this requires choosing the security boundary between fail-closed startup, bounded retry/degrade behavior, provider-specific rate-limit handling, and external resolver responsibility.

options.title: Generic bounded startup policy
options.body: Add a small generic startup retry/backoff or degrade-with-clear-diagnostic policy for active SecretRef provider failures, while keeping provider-specific batching and caching in resolver plugins or wrappers.

options.title: External resolver guidance only
options.body: Keep core fail-fast semantics and document supervisor restart limits plus third-party batching/caching resolvers such as Varlock for 1Password-heavy deployments.

options.title: Configurable retry/circuit breaker
options.body: Add a new `secrets` retry/circuit policy surface with upgrade-safe docs, defaults, and tests, accepting the added configuration and compatibility burden.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup policy
recommendation.body: Add a small generic startup retry/backoff or degrade-with-clear-diagnostic policy for active SecretRef provider failures, while keeping provider-specific batching and caching in resolver plugins or wrappers.

likelyOwner.reason: The core behavior appears to originate in the SecretRef provider and eager runtime activation work authored by joshavant, so they are the best history-backed owner for the policy tradeoff.
